site_description.other: Psychological and ABA support for children and families, with respect for each child’s assent, autonomy and everyday needs.

social_image_alt.other: Keti Petriashvili, Clinical Psychologist — support for children and families

hero_text.other: I help children build useful skills while respecting their comfort, choices and pace. Parents and caregivers are part of the work.

hero_image_alt.other: Illustrative image of Keti Petriashvili supporting a child during a learning activity

intro_text_one.other: A parent or caregiver gives consent, but the child’s assent matters too. I want children to feel safe with me and have a say in what happens to them. When a child is uncomfortable or refuses, I slow down and try to understand why.

intro_text_two.other: I combine psychological understanding with behavioural tools. The question behind every goal is simple: will this make the child’s own life better? I look for progress that helps at home, at school and in the community.

approach_one_text.other: I listen to your concerns and meet your child directly. I look at their strengths, emotions and surroundings, rather than deciding what they need from an adult’s description alone.

approach_two_text.other: We choose measurable goals that make daily life safer, easier or emotionally better. Making a child appear more typical is not the purpose of our work.

approach_three_text.other: Parents can join sessions and practise during ordinary routines. With your permission, I also work with teachers and other professionals when that helps your child.

credentials_intro.other: My background combines clinical psychology, applied behaviour analysis, therapy, supervision and university teaching.

about_lead.other: I’m a clinical psychologist, International Behavior Analyst and lecturer. I work with children and families on the emotional, behavioural and developmental difficulties that affect everyday life.

about_sidebar.other: I offer consultations and welcome professional exchange and international opportunities.

about_story_title.other: Therapy should be ethical and humane

about_story_one.other: I want a child to feel safe with me and, ideally, happy to see me. Their comfort, preferences and willingness to take part matter alongside their parent’s consent. A refusal is a reason to be curious, not automatically another behaviour to remove.

about_story_two.other: I try to understand what the child actually needs, not only what adults expect them to do. We may work in a therapy room, a garden or another everyday setting, depending on what is appropriate and agreed with the family.

about_story_three.other: Parent coaching is part of this work. I involve caregivers where helpful, explain what happened when they cannot join a session, and discuss practical ways to carry support into daily life.

values_title.other: Useful skills, with dignity and trust

value_one_text.other: Every child has a right to a voice, regardless of age, diagnosis, language or intellectual ability. I pay attention to how they communicate agreement, discomfort or the need for a break.

value_two_text.other: I care about how a child feels during therapy and how they see themselves afterward. Learning useful skills should preserve their dignity, bodily autonomy and sense of self.

value_three_text.other: I use measurable goals and look for change beyond our sessions: at home, with other people, in education and in the community. A skill matters when it is useful to the child.

services_title.other: Support for children and the people around them

services_intro.other: I mainly work with children aged around 3–13 and also have experience with adolescents. I support children with autism, ADHD, developmental or behavioural difficulties, as well as emotional and social challenges. A diagnosis is not required.

service_one_text.other: I work with children on emotions, behaviour, communication, coping, relationships and everyday difficulties. The setting and structure depend on the child, not a fixed session format.

service_two_text.other: We explore what may be happening and practise responses you can realistically use at home. Coaching can be a planned conversation or guidance while you interact with your child.

service_three_text.other: With your permission, I may speak with teachers or observe your child in their educational setting. We look at the situation together and find practical ways to offer consistent support.

sessions_first_text.other: I usually meet the parent or caregiver first, without the child, to discuss development, concerns and what you have already tried. Then I meet the child. Together we decide whether I am the right person to help and what support makes sense.

sessions_online_text.other: In-person work is often better for younger children. Online, I may work directly with an older child, with a parent nearby if needed. With younger children, online support often means observing and coaching the parent during real interactions.

sessions_schedule_text.other: Sessions are usually under one hour. We decide the length and frequency from your child’s needs. I do not currently advertise a separate diagnostic assessment service. If another professional would be more helpful, I discuss a referral with you.

experience_autism_text.other: I supervise therapists, review behavioural data and guide individualised intervention plans. My work includes psychological and behavioural support for children and adolescents, in collaboration with families, educators and speech and language professionals.

experience_alte_text.other: I teach Clinical Psychology and Behavioral Science in English in the international undergraduate medical programme, with approximately 200 students per semester. I prepare teaching materials and contribute to the curriculum.

experience_saba_text.other: I teach Applied Behavior Analysis in the bachelor’s programme in psychology and prepare the syllabus, teaching materials and assessments.

experience_trainer_title.other: RBT Training Course Trainer · Tbilisi Autism Center

experience_trainer_text.other: I deliver the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician training course, covering ABA principles, measurement, skill acquisition, behaviour reduction, documentation, professional conduct and ethics.

experience_psychotherapy_title.other: Psychotherapist · Philippe Paumelle French Psychotherapy Center

experience_psychotherapy_text.other: I provided individual psychotherapy to adolescents and adults, including intake assessments, individualised treatment planning and progress monitoring.

experience_counselling_text.other: I provided online counselling for emotional, relational and psychological difficulties.

experience_ari_title.other: Scientific Webinar Interpreter · Autism Research Institute

experience_ari_text.other: I interpret live scientific webinars on autism and co-occurring conditions.

experience_psychosynthesis_title.other: Interpreter and Workshop Assistant · Georgian Institute of Psychosynthesis

experience_psychosynthesis_text.other: I interpret international workshops from English into Georgian, help with organisation and convey the theoretical material accurately.

earlier_clinical.other: My clinical internships included group therapy at Tbilisi No. 1 Psycho-Narcological Rehabilitation Center (April–December 2023) and psychological support in the inpatient psychiatric setting at 5th Clinical Hospital (April–November 2024).

earlier_volunteer.other: I also worked as a Support Worker with Mirabaldebi NGO (July 2021–August 2023) and as a Psychological First Aid Provider with GCRT (November 2024–May 2025).

research_text.other: My research examined cognitive emotion regulation and neuroticism as mediators between childhood trauma and resilience. I analysed data from 318 participants using regression and mediation analyses in SPSS and the PROCESS macro.

languages_text.other: Georgian is my first language. My English qualification is IELTS Academic 8.0, and my German is at A2 level.

writing_title.other: What I want to write about

writing_text.other: I want to write about assent, autonomy and agency: how children communicate yes or no, why refusal should make us curious, and how constant correction can shape a child’s self-esteem. My focus is on helping children learn without sacrificing trust or emotional well-being.
